#### ACRA — Corporate filing and governance

**ACRA XBRL financial statement filing requirements and exemptions** (party in scope: Company)
- **ACRA rule explanation:** The ACRA guidance lists simplified XBRL plus an authorised PDF for smaller and non-publicly accountable companies; XBRL FSH (Banks) or XBRL FSH (Insurance) plus an authorised PDF for the regulated bank, finance and insurance group; PDF only for companies limited by guarantee or companies approved to use other standards; and Full XBRL for all other Singapore-incorporated companies required to file financial statements. “Smaller” requires both current-year revenue and assets not exceeding S$500,000. “Non-publicly accountable” also excludes listed and specified regulated entity types. Maintaining your exemption status
Frequently asked questions (FAQs)
Who qualifies for audit exemption
To qualify for audit exemption as a small company, you need to meet both of these criteria:
Your company is a private company in the financial year; and
Your company meets at least two of these quantitative criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years:
Total annual revenue of $10 million or less, based on your financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards
Total assets of $10 million or less, based on your financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards
50 employees or fewer, based on the number of full-time employees at the end of your financial year
Detailed exemption criteria
If your company is newly incorporated (less than two years old)
You qualify for audit exemption if you meet the criteria in the current financial year.
Example:
First financial year: Check if you are a private company and meet two out of three quantitative criteria that year.
Second financial year: If you did not qualify in the first year, check again using the same requirements for the second year.
If your company is part of a group
You need to meet both of these conditions to qualify for audit exemption:
Your Singapore company or subsidiary qualifies as a small company; and
Your entire group (including foreign entities) meets at least two of these quantitative criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years:
Total annual revenue of $10 million or less, based on your holding company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards
Total assets of $10 million or less, based on your holding company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards
50 employees or fewer, based on the number of full-time employees at the end of your financial year
Note: The audit exemption applies to financial years beginning on or after 1 July 2015.
Maintaining your exemption status
Once your company qualifies as a small company, you remain qualified in subsequent financial years unless:
You cease to be a private company at any time during a financial year; or
You do not meet at least two out of three criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years
Once your group qualifies as a small group, it remains qualified for subsequent financial years. This applies until it does not meet at least two out of three criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years.
Frequently asked questions (FAQs)
Can companies with corporate shareholders get audit exemption?
Yes, you can qualify for audit exemption even if you have corporate shareholders.
Unlike the previous criteria, you do not need to be an exempt private company to qualify for audit exemption.
Does the small company criteria affect financial statement filing?
No, it does not change your financial statement filing requirements.

- **IRAS rule explanation:** IRAS generally disallows input tax on a motor car’s purchase and running costs under regulation 27, unless the vehicle is outside the regulation 25(1) motor-car definition or a specific exception applies. Its examples include qualifying chauffeured pay-per-trip transport services from 1 April 2022; qualifying costs for cars used by a third party from 1 January 2023; and vehicles such as lorries, vans and motorcycles that are not motor cars. All exceptions remain subject to the ordinary claim conditions and records. The input tax incurred in such specific scenarios will be claimable, subject to the conditions for input tax claim.

Updates on 21 May 2026
To further strengthen the retirement adequacy of senior employees, there will be an increase to the CPF contribution rates from 1 Jan 2027. Find out more about these changes and how it affects you and your employees.
Current rates
What are the CPF contribution rates?

View all tables (PDF, 0.2MB) for the full set of contribution rate tables covering all citizenship statuses and SPR years.
Computation
Determine your employees’ CPF contributions
CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee’s citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1)
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5)
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
Different rates apply for different wage bands.
Step 3: Determine the Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
Apply the wage ceilings to determine Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
An employee’s CPF contributions are computed based on the Total Wages payable in a calendar month.
Total Wages are made up of an employee’s Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages. Different ceilings apply to Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages.
Step 4: Compute the CPF contributions on Total Wages
Compute Total CPF contributions
You can compute the total CPF contributions by applying the contribution rate to your employee’s total wages subject to CPF. Please round off the Total CPF contributions to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents, and amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar. The cents should always be dropped for the employee’s share of CPF contributions.

**Public holiday entitlement and pay** (party in scope: Employee)
- **MOM rule explanation:** An Employment Act-covered employee has 11 paid public holidays each year. If a holiday falls on the rest day, the following working day will be a paid public holiday; if it falls on a non-working day, another day off or an extra day at the gross rate is due. Additional basic-rate pay is the default for working on the holiday; substitute-holiday arrangements require mutual agreement. An employee outside Employment Act coverage is governed by the contract. Time off in lieu of hours worked is available only to employees not covered by Part IV under the stated arrangement. Rest-day pay and any excess-hours overtime are separate entitlements. Who qualifies for audit exemption
To qualify for audit exemption as a small company, you need to meet both of these criteria:
Your company is a private company in the financial year; and

Total annual revenue of $10 million or less, based on your financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards

50 employees or fewer, based on the number of full-time employees at the end of your financial year

If your company is newly incorporated (less than two years old)

Second financial year: If you did not qualify in the first year, check again using the same requirements for the second year.

Your Singapore company or subsidiary qualifies as a small company; and
Your entire group (including foreign entities) meets at least two of these quantitative criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years:
Total annual revenue of $10 million or less, based on your holding company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards

50 employees or fewer, based on the number of full-time employees at the end of your financial year

Once your company qualifies as a small company, you remain qualified in subsequent financial years unless:

Yes, you can qualify for audit exemption even if you have corporate shareholders.

**Withholding tax on non-resident service payments** (party in scope: Company)
- **IRAS rule explanation:** IRAS says WHT applies to specified service and management fees paid to a non-resident company to the extent attributable to work done in Singapore; a mixed Singapore/overseas engagement must be apportioned. Services supplied electronically from overseas without sending staff are described as performed outside Singapore. The current page states the prevailing 17% Corporate Income Tax rate on gross service fees for Singapore work, but the applicable DTA, payee residence and permanent-establishment facts may change the rate or treatment. **CPF additional wage ceiling and year-end recalculation** (party in scope: Employer)
- **CPF rule explanation:** CPF Board sets the AW ceiling per employer, per year at S$102,000 less that employee’s Ordinary Wages subject to CPF for the year. The 2026 examples use an OW ceiling of S$8,000 per month and say the year in which an AW is due and payable controls the ceiling. In the last month of employment or December, whichever is earlier, recalculate using actual OW subject to CPF through that period; pay any CPF shortfall with the last-month or December contributions, and apply for a refund if excess CPF contributions result. $102,000 - Total Ordinary Wages (OW) subject to CPF for the year

$102,000 – ($8,000* x 12)
* The OW ceiling is capped at $8,000 for 2026.

ceiling based on the actual OW subject to CPF paid up till the last month of employment or in December and pay any shortfall in CPF contributions

- **MOM rule explanation:** An Employment Act-covered employee becomes entitled to paid annual leave after at least 3 months; being on probation does not remove that entitlement.
